page: Google Cloud Platform z4m-highmem-192 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on an x86_64 processor architecture. The configuration supplies 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 1488.0 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to approximately 7.75 GB of memory per core. The hardware profile does not include GPU acceleration hardware.

A central component of the z4m-highmem-192 is its high-capacity direct-attached storage subsystem. The instance comes equipped with 180,389 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 12 local SSD drives. Network provisions include zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, aligning the instance with private enterprise network deployments.

The hardware configuration achieves high resource density by matching high compute parallelism and large system memory with hundreds of terabytes of local solid-state storage. In terms of cost efficiency, operating this instance requires sustained demand across all three resource dimensions; workloads that do not saturate the local NVMe throughput or utilize the broad 192-thread architecture risk leaving substantial hardware capacity idle.

The z4m-highmem-192 is suited for data-intensive enterprise workloads requiring extreme local disk capacity and low-latency storage access. Target use cases include large-scale distributed NoSQL and relational databases, real-time analytics clusters, high-volume ETL pipelines, and high-throughput data warehousing nodes.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4m-highmem-192 is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for high-throughput, data-heavy computing. Powered by an x86_64 architecture with 192 dedicated vCPUs, it features 1488.0 GB of system RAM, providing an allocation of 7.75 GB per core. The server includes an integrated local storage array totaling 180,389 GB across 12 local NVMe SSDs, delivering massive direct-attached non-volatile capacity without reliance on network storage. There are no attached GPUs, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. From an efficiency standpoint, the instance balances high compute density and large memory capacity against an extraordinary volume of low-latency local storage. This configuration requires sustained, high-IOPS operational loads to prevent resource underutilization. The z4m-highmem-192 is particularly suited for large-scale distributed databases, extensive data warehouse nodes, transactional systems, and high-volume ETL workloads requiring local NVMe staging.
